20844-critical-miscellanies-vol-3-of-3-e:
Erasmus was a man of wide reading, yet not a scholar in the strict sense. John Morley borrows that verdict in his essay on Pattison's Memoirs, in Critical Miscellanies. Mark Pattison, an Oxford rector, left memoirs of a keen, questing mind.

Morley weighs Pattison's learning, doubt, and lonely search for truth. Oxford in ferment, church strife, and books fill the backdrop. The essay blends life study with literary judgment in Morley's crisp style. Readers who like Victorian essays at their most thoughtful will find a sharp mind judging a kindred one here.
doe-osti-3002982-a-latent-variable-formu:
Carlos Llosa-Vite, Daniel M. Dunlavy, and Richard B. Lehoucq of Sandia, with Oscar López and Arvind Prasadan, reframe a tensor model in report SAND2025-14005R. The model is the Poisson canonical polyadic tensor model, used for count data arranged in multiway tables. Their trick is a latent-variable view: the observed tensor is what remains after hiding one dimension of a larger random tensor.

From that view, the authors derive maximum-likelihood estimators for the model. They show that several well-known fitting algorithms for nonnegative matrix and tensor factorization are really expectation-maximization algorithms in disguise. They also derive the observed and expected Fisher information matrices. Those matrices reveal how tensor rank affects identifiability, whether the data can pin down the factors at all. Rank-one models simplify greatly.
doe-osti-3816540-statistical-correlation:
National Laboratory of the Rockies report NLR/TP-5700-101179, dated September 2026, links solar mirror aim errors to wind strength. Matthew Emes, Devon Kesseli, Matthew Neber, and Stephanie Meyen are the printed authors. Heliostats steer sunbeams onto a tower receiver, and wind pushes their facets off aim. Published field data on that drift are sparse. The team set a laser test at the lab's Flatirons Campus platform. A camera watched the beam spot wander on a grid target while gauges logged each gust.

Side-to-side drift grew with peak wind speed along a logarithmic curve. Up-and-down drift grew faster, along an exponential curve. Both also fit the square-of-speed curve expected from wind load physics. Which pattern rules depends on the mirror's frame design. Next steps call for more field runs to split gravity sag from wind push. The work sits inside the Heliostat Consortium's field task.
nasa-tm-19690019484-a-procedure-for-furn:
Thomas J. Moore and Donald W. Adams of Lewis Research Center wrote this June 1969 memorandum, TM X-1815. They give a procedure for joining tungsten-uranium dioxide cermet cylinders with furnace brazed butt joints, at three thousand degrees Celsius. Such heat-proof cylinders serve high-temperature nuclear work. The joint had to fill completely, with no defects and little excess braze metal.

Brazing in helium with a tungsten-osmium alloy joined the cylinder's lengthwise seam successfully, they report. The team also tried alloy placement methods, cylinder orientations, and two alternate alloys briefly. One cost appeared: the heat cycle cut the parent material's strength by about a fifth. Larger tungsten grains explain the loss, they judge, and a later heat treatment removed an unwanted phase from the braze.
podcast-dannyjones-DCenM4t7soI:
Decorated SEAL veteran Kristin Beck joins Danny Jones for KONCRETE number 59. Beck served over twenty years on three SEAL teams, including Team 6. She deployed thirteen times to Bosnia, Iraq, and Afghanistan.

Beck earned more than fifty ribbons across seven combat tours. The title names her later life as a transgender woman. Jones traces the path from elite warrior to public advocate. Beck speaks about duty, identity, and the cost of both lives. The episode offers a rare long talk with a soldier whose story crosses two worlds. Her candor makes the hour stand out.
